places.name: The Capital Empire
places.note: Apartment-style hotel in Sandton, the modern business heart of Jozi. Used both nights either side of the safari — easy to and from O.R. Tambo.

places.name: Nelson Mandela Square
places.note: Plaza in Sandton with the giant Madiba statue and the Sandton City mall — a useful walk-around if you have an hour to kill before dinner.

places.name: Bukhara
places.note: Indian restaurant on Nelson Mandela Square — best curry in Sandton and an easy first-night dinner after the long flights.

places.name: The Butcher Shop & Grill
places.note: Steakhouse on Nelson Mandela Square. South Africa is a beef country — the dry-aged ribeye is the move.

places.name: &Beyond Ngala Safari Lodge
places.note: Colonial-style lodge in the 14,700-hectare &Beyond Ngala Private Game Reserve, sharing an unfenced border with Kruger National Park. Twenty thatched cottages, expert ranger-and-tracker teams, open-air boma dinners. Highlight of the trip.

places.name: Greater Kruger / Sabi Sand
places.note: South Africa's flagship wilderness — Big Five country: lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, rhino. Best accessed via a private concession (Ngala, Sabi Sand, Timbavati) rather than the public park self-drive.

places.name: Hoedspruit Airport (HDS)
places.note: Tiny gateway airport in Limpopo — one-hour Airlink hop from Johannesburg, ~45-minute transfer from there to Ngala. Open-air arrivals, a literal thatched roof. The trip begins the moment you land.

places.name: Primi Seacastle
places.note: Tiny boutique hotel right on Camps Bay's beach strip — Table Mountain behind, the Atlantic out the window. First-leg base in Cape Town.

places.name: Fairways On The Bay
places.note: Eight-room guesthouse a hundred meters from Camps Bay Beach. Used as the second Cape Town base after the Garden Route loop. Quieter than the strip.

places.name: Table Mountain
places.note: The flat-topped icon. You can ride the cableway up in clear weather, or hike one of the routes from Kirstenbosch. Plan for a clear morning before the famous "tablecloth" of cloud rolls in.

places.name: Skeleton Gorge / Nursery Ravine Hike
places.note: The classic Table Mountain hike from the back, starting in Kirstenbosch. 5–6 hours up Skeleton Gorge and down Nursery Ravine. Go with a guide from Hike Table Mountain — they know the weather windows.

places.name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
places.note: World-class botanical garden on the eastern slopes of Table Mountain. Plan a slow afternoon: the Boomslang treetop canopy walk, the protea section, lunch at the tea room. Sunset concerts on summer Sundays.

places.name: Cape of Good Hope
places.note: The southwestern tip of Africa — wild fynbos cliffs, baboons, and Cape Point lighthouse. Best done as a full-day loop along the peninsula, ideally with a local driver who knows the timing.

places.name: Cape Point Tour w/ Lynette
places.note: Eight-hour private guided loop down the Cape Peninsula — Chapman's Peak, the Cape of Good Hope, Boulders penguins, Simon's Town lunch. Lynette at Exquisite Cape Tours runs the best version of this day.

places.name: Boulders Penguin Colony
places.note: A wild colony of ~2,000 African penguins on a beach in Simon's Town. Combines neatly with the Cape Point loop.

places.name: Robben Island
places.note: The prison where Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years. Half-day tour by ferry from the V&A Waterfront, guided by a former political prisoner. Book in advance — tours fill weeks ahead.

places.name: Bo-Kaap
places.note: Cape Malay neighborhood of brightly painted cobblestone houses on the slopes of Signal Hill. Walk it on a Sunday morning; pop into the Bo-Kaap Museum.

places.name: V&A Waterfront
places.note: Working harbour redeveloped into the city's main eating, shopping, and ferry hub. The V&A Food Market is a quick lunch; the Zeitz MOCAA contemporary-art museum is worth an hour.

places.name: Lion's Head
places.note: Conical peak next to Table Mountain — much shorter hike, panoramic 360 views at the top. Locals do it for sunrise or full-moon sunsets.

places.name: Kloof Street House
places.note: Victorian house turned colonial-meets-trendy restaurant on Kloof Street. Outdoor deck under fairy lights — perfect first-night Cape Town dinner.

places.name: The Codfather
places.note: Camps Bay seafood and sushi institution — pick your fish off the ice. No menus; the staff walks you through what came in that day.

places.name: The Bungalow
places.note: Glass-front Clifton beach club at sunset — sundowner cocktails on the deck overhanging the Atlantic. Reserve. The food is fine; the view is the meal.

places.name: The Pot Luck Club
places.note: Luke Dale Roberts's top-of-the-silo small-plates spot at the Old Biscuit Mill in Woodstock. 360 views, tasting-menu format. Book weeks ahead.

places.name: La Colombe
places.note: Tasting-menu fine dining in a forest setting in Constantia. Consistently in South Africa's top 3 restaurants. Long lunch territory; book months ahead.

places.name: Azure at The Twelve Apostles
places.note: Cliffside restaurant at the Twelve Apostles Hotel, between Camps Bay and Llandudno. The drive down the coast is half the experience.

places.name: Savoy Cabbage
places.note: Long-running farm-to-table bistro in the CBD — known for the tomato tart and ostrich carpaccio.

places.name: Eastern Food Bazaar
places.note: Cheap-and-cheerful pan-Asian food hall on Longmarket Street — biryani, curry, dosas. Lunch territory.

places.name: Stellenbosch Wine Tour (Wine Flies)
places.note: Ten-hour small-group day tour from Cape Town through four or five working wineries — Stellenbosch, Franschhoek, sometimes Paarl. Cheese pairings, a long lunch, local guides. Don't try to drive yourself.

places.name: Stellenbosch (town)
places.note: South Africa's second-oldest European settlement — Cape Dutch architecture under oak trees, art galleries, university-town energy. Stop in town between wineries.

places.name: Cape Winelands
places.note: Stellenbosch + Franschhoek + Paarl are the historic three. Old estates on dramatic mountain backdrops; the wine is genuinely world-class and the prices are a fraction of California.

places.name: L'Agulhas
places.note: Southernmost tip of the African continent — where the Atlantic and Indian Oceans officially meet. There's a marker stone, a lighthouse, and not much else; that's the point. Easy detour from the Cape Town–Garden Route drive.

places.name: Sea Shack Struisbaai
places.note: Beach shack right on the dunes outside L'Agulhas — fresh fish and chips at picnic tables in the sand. Lunch stop on the drive east.

places.name: Augusta Bay of Knysna
places.note: Small guest house perched above Knysna Lagoon with views to the Knysna Heads. Breakfast in the atrium, walking distance to the waterfront.

places.name: Knysna Heads
places.note: Two sandstone cliffs that form the dramatic mouth of Knysna Lagoon — one of the most beautiful estuaries in the country. Park at the East Head Café for the classic view.

places.name: Margaret's Viewpoint
places.note: Quiet pullout above Knysna with a sweeping view down the lagoon — better than the postcards, and almost always empty.

places.name: East Head Café
places.note: Knysna brunch institution literally cantilevered over the Heads. The Knysna oysters are local; the view is the meal.

places.name: Freshline Fisheries
places.note: Working fish co-op at the Knysna Waterfront — buy a paper cone of fresh calamari or hake-and-chips and eat it on the dock.

places.name: JJ's Restaurant
places.note: Knysna Quays dinner spot — steaks, seafood, candlelit waterfront tables.

places.name: Monkeyland & Birds of Eden
places.note: Free-roaming primate sanctuary and the world's largest free-flight aviary, side by side outside Plett. Tickets cover both; allow 2–3 hours.

places.name: Jukani Wildlife Sanctuary
places.note: Big-cat sanctuary on the same N2 stretch as Monkeyland — lions, tigers, leopards, cheetahs rescued from the wildlife trade. Conservation-first, no cub petting. Combine all three on one Plett afternoon.

places.name: Plett Beachfront Accommodation
places.note: Self-catering apartments steps from Central Beach in Plettenberg Bay. Walk to dinner, walk to the beach, that's the brief.

places.name: Robberg Nature Reserve
places.note: Five-hour clifftop loop on a rocky peninsula outside Plett — dolphins below, fur seals at the point, fynbos and sea everywhere. The signature Garden Route walk. Pack water and lunch.

places.name: Plettenberg Bay
places.note: Resort town on the east end of the Garden Route — long beaches, southern right whales offshore in winter, plus the Crags wildlife sanctuaries 15 minutes east.

places.name: The Lookout Deck
places.note: Open-deck restaurant on the Plett headland with a 180-degree bay view — the spot for whale-watching with a glass of wine in your hand.

places.name: Emily Moon River Lodge
places.note: African-fusion restaurant on a wooden deck over the Bitou River, just inland of Plett. Eclectic decor, very long sunsets.

places.name: Clare's Cakes & Coffee
places.note: Tiny Plett bakery for a breakfast pastry and a packed lunch box to take on the Robberg hike.
